newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen complaining to Pakistan over aircraft.
newsitem.headline: India seen complaining to Pakistan over aircraft.

text.p: India was expected to lodge a complaint with Pakistan after several recent intrusions into Indian air space by remote-controlled aircraft, a Defence Ministry official said on Thursday.
Indian Air Force planes on Wednesday morning fired at a small, pilotless plane which had crossed into the western state of Gujarat from Pakistan, a Defence Ministry spokesman said.
It was not known if the aircraft, called a Remotely Piloted Vehicle (RPV), had been hit, the spokesman said.
"There have been some intrusions in the last couple of days in the Southwest Air Command region by remotely controlled pilotless aircraft," the spokesman said.
"We believe this is the first occasion such aircraft have been involved in such incidents."

Indian forces in the region of the alleged intrusion near Bhuj airport, 300 km (190 miles) from the Gujarat state capital of Ahmedabad, had been put on alert and were searching for the aircraft, he said.
The region lies between Bombay and Karachi near the Arabian Sea. It was not known how many Indian Air Force jets were involved in the shooting or what weapons were used.

"The Ministry of External Affairs will probably take it up with Pakistan," the Defence Ministry spokesman said. Foreign Ministry officials and diplomats at the Pakistani High Commission (embassy) in New Delhi were not immediately available for comment.
"We have taken suitable air defence measures," the Defence Ministry spokesman said without elaborating.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since they were carved out of British India in 1947.

Troops on both sides of the frontier regularly fire on each other in the disputed northern region of Kashmir, which was the cause of two of the three wars. The rest of the long border is closely monitored.
The Hindu newspaper said the RPVs which crossed into Indian air space had sensors and night vision devices used for surveillance.

"The 'live' data which they can transmit is vital for directing surface-to-surface missiles towards static and moving targets, such as airfields and tank columns during battle," the daily newspaper said.

The pilot of a Lufthansa jet reported earlier this week that an unidentified aircraft passed within 300 feet (90 metres) as the planes flew over Moga, about 300 km (190 miles) northwest of New Delhi near the Pakistan border, an official of the Air Traffic Controllers Guild told Reuters.
The Lufthansa Boeing 747 was flying from New Delhi to Frankfurt on Sunday morning, a senior guild official said.

"It could have been a Pakistani aircraft intruding into Indian air space," said the air traffic control official, who asked not to be named. He said the Indian Air Force was investigating the reported near miss.
